Figure size for a table-style subgroup forest plot

Source: R/plot_subgroup_forest.R
subgroup_forest_size.Rd

The width and height, in inches, to draw plot_subgroup_forest() at: the width fits its text columns and forest panel, and the height gives each row row_height. In Quarto, compute it in an earlier chunk and pass it as fig-width: !expr size[["width"]] and fig-height: !expr size[["height"]] (chunk options are evaluated before the chunk's own code runs).

Usage

subgroup_forest_size(
  data,
  effect_size,
  ci_low,
  ci_high,
  ...,
  text_size = 8,
  row_height = 0.115 * text_size/7,
  axis_height = 0.45 * text_size/7
)

Arguments

data, effect_size, ci_low, ci_high

As for plot_subgroup_forest().

...

Other arguments passed to plot_subgroup_forest(). Those that change the layout (subgroup, level, group_col, n_col, events_col, pvalue_col, ref_col, estimate_digits, ref_label, labels, font_family, forest_width, gap_level, gap_subgroup) must match; the others are ignored, so the same arguments can be passed to both functions.

text_size

Numeric. Text size, in points, as for plot_subgroup_forest(). Default 8.

row_height

Numeric. Height of one row, in inches. Default 0.115 * text_size / 7, scaling with the text.

axis_height

Numeric. Height of the estimate axis and the plot margins, in inches. Default 0.45 * text_size / 7, scaling with the text.

Value

Named numeric vector: width and height, in inches.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
    subgroup = c("Overall", "Age", "Age"),
    level = c("", "<65", "65+"),
    hr = c(0.80, 0.75, 0.85),
    lcl = c(0.70, 0.60, 0.72),
    ucl = c(0.92, 0.94, 1.01)
)
size <- subgroup_forest_size(df, "hr", "lcl", "ucl")
p <- plot_subgroup_forest(df, "hr", "lcl", "ucl")
# ggplot2::ggsave("forest.png", p, width = size[["width"]],
#     height = size[["height"]])
